shown.message:
I answered all six items on `experiment-repo`#5, closed it, and pushed the new analyses to `main` of experiment-repo (`c3b42a9`). The reply gives either "confirmed" or exact replacement wording per item. Most quoted numbers match the code and CSVs, and where the text overstates I said so.

The corrections that change what the paper can claim:
- **Chernoff numbers:** `bound_check.py` used ranks (5 / 6 / 1) that differ from the main runs. At the main runs' fold-median ranks the sufficient k is 506 / 742 / 171 / 459, not 551 / 742 / 57 / 459. The "35 of 35 rows" check is trivially true because the Chernoff value is 1.0 in every row. The risk bound is 1.6–2.7 times above the measured mean at k=30 on the MTEB pools, and below it only up to k≤3 (MTEB-Eng) and k≤8 (MTEB-Multi).
- **Later-release penalty:** on the same test models it is +9% at k=3 on MTEB-Eng, with an interval that includes 0. On MTEB-Multi it is +18%. The paper's 18% and 25% compare different test sets.
- **Strongest-quintile bias:** about 40% of the MTEB bias is an artefact of grouping by a score that contains the targets. Grouping by the observed scores leaves −0.06 to −0.07. On MTEB-Eng that remainder is not significant.
- **Predictor comparison:** the factor model is not better than ridge, Ledoit-Wolf or the best simple predictor on the MTEB pools. It beats only kNN on HELM.
- **Pool construction:**
  - MTEB-Multi includes English tasks and overlaps MTEB-Eng heavily (111 of 117 models, 69 of 70 tasks), so the two are not separate pools.
  - The identity-versus-logit choice is made once per pool, not on each fold's training rows.
  - The reference the paper calls an optimistic bound is not one: on MTEB-Eng the in-sample reference (0.479) is higher than the held-out LOBO reference (0.470).

I also fixed a defect of mine in `aggregate.py`: the organisation-grouped bootstrap clustered by the finer family, and its family count was mislabelled. Only `results/robustness.csv` changed, so Table A3's organisation-grouped rows need regenerating.

I opened `figtab-repo`#4 for that, plus the rank notes on Tables 1–3 and the baseline note on Table A5. `paper-repo` now has to change the text.

The reply covers all six items. The per-item details came from my earlier checks, which I could only recover from notes after the context reset. I did not re-run every one of them this turn. These are the ones to look at first:
- the run-time ranges and the 100-draw robustness variants (item 6)
- the maximum-variance selector wording (item 2)

I did not update issue #3, since the plan has not changed.
